r0051: 26.  The Court reiterates that an interference must strike a “fair balance” between the demands of the general interest of the community and the requirements of the protection of the individual’s fundamental rights. The concern to achieve this balance is reflected in the structure of Article 1 as a whole, including therefore the second paragraph thereof: there must be a reasonable relationship of proportionality between the means employed and the aim pursued. In determining whether this requirement is met, the Court recognises that the State enjoys a wide margin of appreciation with regard both to choosing the means of enforcement and to ascertaining whether the consequences of enforcement are justified in the general interest for the purpose of achieving the object of the law in question. In spheres such as housing, which plays a central role in the welfare and economic policies of modern societies, the Court will respect the legislature’s judgment in that regard unless that judgment is manifestly without reasonable foundation (see Immobiliare Saffi, cited above, § 49).
r0052: 27.  The applicant disputed the legitimacy of the aim of the laws in question. In substance, he submitted that the absence of an effective State housing policy had deprived him of his right to dispose of his apartment, by favouring exclusively the interests of the tenant. In particular, the system providing for exceptions to the suspension of the enforcement of evictions was wholly ineffective. While it was true that it was possible in theory to ask the enforcement judge (*juge de l’exécution*) to rule that the suspension of enforcement did not apply to a situation in which the tenant was in arrears with the rent, which would give the eviction priority, the need in practice to institute proceedings for that purpose, which in his case had lasted approximately two years, rendered the system inoperative. Furthermore, the legislative system afforded him no means of reacting so as to protect his interests.
r0053: 28.  The Government submitted that the legislative measures in question had pursued an aim in the general interest, namely the protection of tenants, in view of the housing crisis affecting the largest urban centres and the difficulty of adequately rehousing tenants of modest means who were facing eviction; in the present case, the tenant had a very modest income (ITL 577,000, that is, less than two thousand French francs per month) and had a dependent child.
r0054: 29.  The Government further observed that many leases had expired in the years 1982-1983; the simultaneous enforcement of all those leases would have caused serious social tension. The measures in question had therefore been intended to protect public order. The Government also observed that the staggering of the provision of police assistance had proved necessary in view of the impossibility of guaranteeing such assistance to everyone at the same time.
r0055: 30.  Lastly, the Government observed that the emergency provisions concerning the suspension or staggering of the enforcement of evictions had provided for exceptions under which, in particular, landlords could obtain enforcement of evictions with police assistance where, as in the present case, their tenant was in arrears with the rent or the service charges for a total amount equivalent to two months’ rent. The Government emphasised that in the present case the Prefect had granted police assistance immediately after being informed that the eviction had priority.
r0056: 31.  The Court considers that, in adopting emergency measures providing for the suspension of evictions and laying down certain exceptions to their application, the Italian legislature could reasonably have considered that the means chosen were appropriate for achieving the legitimate aim (see, mutatis mutandis, Scollo v. Italy, judgment of 28 September 1995, Series A no. 315-C, § 40).
r0057: 32.  It remains to be determined, however, whether in the present case a fair balance was struck between the interests of the community and the rights of property owners, and of the applicant in particular.
